description: Customized, one-time, high-emotion purchase. Opaque prices, plentiful alternatives, zero buyer leverage and zero time. The buyer describes what she wants once; the agents shop and haggle across channels (boutique / sample sale / resale / DTC).

narrowedScenario.summary: Bride, US 8, wedding ~4 months out (too tight for 6-9mo custom). Wants a specific designer look. Agents gather comparable gowns across three channels that genuinely haggle (boutique floor-sample / sample sale, preowned resale, DTC made-to-order), then negotiate price + strip alterations/add-ons against a real cross-channel BATNA.
whyThisScenario: Opaque pricing: boutiques rarely quote over the phone, so the 'stonewaller' style is real and demoable (extract a range or a firm callback).
Real comparables: the same/near-identical gown exists across boutique, sample sale, resale and DTC, so the BATNA is honest and clickable.
Deadline pressure: a ~4-month date rules out 6-9mo custom and makes lead-time-vs-date a live negotiation lever.
Hidden-fee stack: alterations ($150-$700+, ~20-30% of gown price) and rush fees are a concrete red flag the agent itemizes and strips.

buyerPersona.note: Target ~ off-the-rack/made-to-order low tier; reservation ~ made-to-order median; walkaway ~ regional high-cost median.

specFields.prompt: What silhouette are you looking for?
When is the wedding? (drives the lead-time hard constraint)
Open to sample-sale or preowned to save, or new-only?
Any fabric preference (satin, lace, tulle, crepe)?
Sleeve style (strapless, long sleeve, cap, off-shoulder)?
A specific designer/style in mind (e.g. Pronovias, Maggie Sottero)?
Any customization (custom measurements, added sleeves, color change)?

priceBenchmark.source: The Knot 2026 Real Weddings Study (10,474 US couples, $2,100 avg gown); Zola 2026 ($2,250); dreamdresses 2026 channel breakdown; Stillwhite/Nearly Newlywed resale 2026.
priceBenchmark.note: Blended national average across channels. Use the per-channel subtype bands below for red-flag detection; the blended median is only a fallback.

dress_resale.source: Stillwhite (102k+ listings) / Nearly Newlywed 2026; 50-80% of retail

dress_custom.source: The Knot custom cost 2026 ($3,000-$4,000 start); 19% of brides

leadTime.note: Wedding date is a HARD constraint. Made-to-order production is the longest single stage; alterations need a buffer on top.

redFlags.message: Quote is 25%+ above the channel median — possible 'wedding markup'. 28% of vendors quote higher when 'wedding' is mentioned vs an identical non-wedding event (Consumer Reports 2016, 40 vendors, 12 states; markups commonly 20-50%).

Total is inflated by alterations/veil/rush/preservation baked in. Alterations run $150-$700 typical (~20-30% of the gown, $700-$1,500+ on beaded gowns); rush fees add $25+/service under ~3 weeks. Itemize and strip; an independent seamstress is often cheaper for equal work.
redFlags.source: The Knot / Zola / RobeMarie / Alteration Specialists 2026

redFlags.message: Resale/DTC quote 30%+ below channel median — verify authenticity, real photos, exact measurements, condition, and return policy before trusting. Common in dropship knock-offs and misrepresented listings.

No returns / final sale on a made-to-order or resale gown magnifies sizing and misrepresentation risk — flag it and require exact measurements or a return window (e.g. Nearly Newlywed offers a 5-day return for a $50 fee).
Lead time unstated or 'it depends' against a firm wedding date — pin down a firm ship-by that leaves an 8-10 week alterations buffer, or walk. Production alone runs 4-8 months for made-to-order.

negotiationLevers.description: Buy the tried-on sample / sample-sale gown: 30-70% off retail. Biggest single lever.
Decline in-house alterations/veil/rush; use an independent seamstress — removes 20-30% of the total.
A real resale/DTC/other-boutique quote on the same or comparable gown is honest BATNA leverage worth ~15-25%.
Off-peak buying (non-May/Oct, slow-season boutique) is 10-20% softer.
Cash / full prepay vs deposit + card — 5-15% on slower-moving inventory.
Free/discounted shipping or a written price-match on a listed gown.

notes: Haggling a brand-new full-price boutique gown is uncommon and often rebuffed; leverage lives in channel choice (sample/resale/DTC) and in stripping add-ons, not in demanding a raw discount on a new gown.
Sample sales: 30-70% off (display models; expect minor wear + immediate alterations).
Deposits are standard; made-to-order is usually final sale.
Always get an itemized, all-in quote in writing (gown + alterations + rush + shipping).

callListSource.query: bridal boutique OR wedding dress shop
callListSource.note: Boutiques + David's Bridal for phone/voice legs. Also DTC online sellers (Azazie, Lulus) via customer-service lines, and resale marketplaces (Stillwhite, Nearly Newlywed, Kleinfeld Again) where individual sellers message and genuinely haggle.

channels.note: Appointment-gated; often refuses phone pricing → target for the stonewaller demo.
Fast, cheap made-to-order substitutes; strong BATNA floor.
Individual sellers haggle directly → best 'real moving price' leg.

counterpartyStyles.description: Holds firm on price, pushes deposits, tests whether the buyer is serious.
'We only give pricing after an in-store appointment' — must extract a range or a firm callback.
Bundles alterations, veils, rush fees, preservation; inflates the total. Agent must itemize and strip non-essentials.
